doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Parents' reaction to her career
summary: Her parents found her path a mystery but were happy she did what she wanted.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your parents support you in your eventual choice to become a jazz musician?

Well you know I think I was kind of a mystery to them, what it was that I was doing. But you know I’m sure they were happy that I was doing what I wanted to do. That was probably the most important thing to them. They didn’t entirely understand it but you know that’s the way it goes.
And how does your mother describe to other people what you do?
I don’t know you’ll have to ask her, you’ll have to ask her. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
